# Load balancer 502 from idle-timeout mismatch with backend

Users occasionally get an error on long-lived requests; retrying works.

The backend's keep-alive timeout (60s) was shorter than the load balancer's idle timeout (75s), so the backend closed connections the LB still considered open, producing 502s on reused connections.

1. Correlate 502s with connection reuse near the 60s mark
2. Set the backend keep-alive timeout higher than the LB idle timeout
3. Reload and confirm the premature-close errors stop
4. Document the timeout ordering rule (backend > LB idle)

Error Details
```
HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway; nginx: 'upstream prematurely closed connection while reading response header'; backend keep-alive 60s vs LB idle 75s
```

Tags: networking, load-balancer, 502, keep-alive, idle-timeout
